FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Imiprothrin, technical is used in the preparation of insecticidal formulations for agricultural use. 

Imiprothrin is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for a 
mixture of 20 percent 2,5-dioxo-3-prop-2-ynylimidazolidin-1-ylmethyl (1R,35)-2,2-dimethyl-3-(2-methylprop- 
l-enyl) cyclopropanecarboxylate and 80 percent 2,5-dioxo-3-prop-2-ynylimidazolidin-1-ylmethyl (1R,3R)-2,2- 
dimethyl-3-(2-methylprop-1-enyl) cyclopropane carboxylate. 


The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of imiprothrin are given below: 


Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass 
C,,H,,N,O, [1R, 3S] - isomer 318.37

In formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and, 
the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IMIPROTHRIN TECHNICAL — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for Imiprothrin, technical. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title 
1070: 1992 Reagent grade water — Specification 
(third revision) 
6940: 1982 Methods of test for pesticides and 


their formulations ( first revision) 


8190 (Part 1) Requirements for packing of 

: 1988 pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides 
(second revision) 

10946: 1996 Methods of sampling for technical 


grade pesticides ( first revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of clear, homogeneous, 
yellow coloured liquid. It shall be free from extraneous 
impurities. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 


requirements given in Table 1. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in tin container. The 
containers shall also meet the general requirements 
given in IS 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall be securely closed and, the 
following information shall be marked legibly and 
indelibly on each container in addition to any other 
information as is necessary under the /nsecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net Quantity; 

g) Nominal Imiprothrin content, percent (m/m); 


h) Cautionary notice worded as in the /nsecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder; and 


j) Any other information required under the 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark.

5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and 
the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details 
of the conditions under which the licence for use of 
the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


6 SAMPLING 


Representative sample ofthe material shall be drawn as 
prescribed in IS 10946. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred to 
in col 4 and 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis.

ANNEXA 
[ Table 1, Item (i) ] 


DETERMINATION OF IMIPROTHRIN CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Imiprothrin content is determined by gas 
chromatography by using internal standard technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 Gas Liquid Chromatograph (GLC), equipped 
with Flame Ionization Detector (FID) and, coupled to a 
printer-plotter-cum-integrator or PC based data system 
is used for this determination. The suggested operative 
parameters are as follows, but can be changed, if 
necessary provided standardization is done: 


Column : DB-608 megabore column 
(or equivalent, viz. DB- 
1301 and DB-624), 30 m 


length, 0.53mm ID, 1.5 um 


thickness or equivalent 
column. 
Temperature conditions : Oven — 240°C 


Injection port — 250°C 
Detector — 260°C 


Gases and corresponding flow rates : 


a) Nitrogen (carrier) — 4 ml/min 

b) Hydrogen — 30 ml/min 

c) Air (FID) — 300 ml/min 
Volume injected : Tul 


A-2.2 Microlitre Syringe 
A-2.3 Standard Glassware 
A-3 REAGENTS 


A-3.1 Chloroform — AR grade or equivalent. 


A-3.2 Internal Standard — Dicyclohexyl phthalate — 
AR grade or equivalent. 


A-3.3 Imiprothrin Reference Standard — Of known 
purity. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh about 200 mg of dicyclohexyl phthalate into 
a 50 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in chloroform and 
make up the volume upto the mark with chloroform. 
Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh about 200 mg of imiprothrin reference standard 
of known purity into a 25 ml standard flask. Add 5 ml of 
dicyclohexyl phthalate (internal standard) solution and 
make up the volume upto the mark with chloroform. If 
necessary, dilute suitably and inject the solution 1 ul in 
GC-FID and record the peak area. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh a quantity of a sample equivalent to 200 mg of 
imiprothrin into a 25 ml volumetric flask. Add 5 ml of 
dicyclohexyl phthalate (internal standard) solution and 
make up the volume upto the mark with chloroform. If 
necessary, dilute suitably and inject the solution 1 ul 
in GC-FID and record the peak area under curve for 
standard and internal standard. 


A-5 ESTIMATION 


A-5.1 Inject 1 ul of reference standard solution until the 
area quotients of internal standard/ reference standard 
of two successive chromatograms do not deviate 
from each other by more than 2 percent. Then use the 
following injection sequence: 


pt Sp Sp C, Sp SO, ---.+. 


where, 
C = standard solution, and; 
S = sample solution (1, 2, ...... ‚n). 


From the chromatograms of the standard solution 
sample solution, measure the peak areas of the internal 
standard and imiprothrin peaks, and compute the 
percentage of imiprothrin as given in A-6. 


A-5.2 


Imiprothrin 


Retention Times (Guide Values) 
: 3.4 min (approximately) 


Dicyclohexyl Phthalate : 6.3 min (approximately) 
(Internal Standard) 


Total run time : 10 min

internal standard is given in Fig. 1

ANNEXB 
[ Table 1, Item (11) ] 


DETERMINATION OF IR ISOMER RATIO 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


The IR isomer ratio in imiprothrin is determined 
using a chiral HPLC column, which separates the 
isomers. The percentage of each isomer is calculated 
from the areas of the peaks observed in the HPLC 
estimation. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 A High Performance Liquid Chromatography 
system, equipped with UV detectorandchromatographic 
software/printer plotter-cum-integrator or PC based 
data system is used for this determination. The 
suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can 
be changed, if necessary, provided standardization is 
done: 


Column Chiral OA-2000 or DNP-2000 
(or equivalent), 25 cm x 4 mm ID. 
particle size 5 um or equivalent 
column (two column in series) 

Temperature Ambient 

Mobile phase hexane dichloromethane 
acetonitrile (70 : 29: 1 v/v) 

Flow rate 1.3 ml/min 

Injection volume: 20 ml 


Detector Ultraviolet detector (230 nm) 


B-2.2 Analytical Balance — With an accuracy of 
0.1 mg 


B-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 25 ul 
B-2.3 Standard Glassware 


B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 Imiprothrin Technical Sample, having all the 
Four Isomers 


B-3.2 Hexane — HPLC/AR grade. 
B-3.3 Dichloromethane — HPLC/AR grade. 
B-3.4 Acetonitrile — HPLC/AR grade. 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


B-4.1 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh about 100 mg of imiprothrin, technical sample 
into a 10 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in mobile phase 
and make up the volume upto the mark with mobile 
phase. Shake well to homogenize. 


B-4.2 Preparation of Technical Reference Sample 
Solution 


Weigh accurately 100 mg of imiprothrin technical 
reference sample into a 10 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve 
in mobile phase and make up the volume upto the mark 
with mobile phase. Shake well to homogenize. 


B-5 ESTIMATION 


B-5.1 Inject 20 ul solution of imiprothrin technical 
reference sample in HPLC and identify qualitatively all 
the four isomers. 


B-5.2 Inject 20 ul solution in HPLC to analyze the 
(1R) — Isomer ratio. Note the areas of different 
isomers. Calculate the percentage of active and inactive 
isomers in the sample as indicated under B-6. 


B-5.3 Retention Time (Guide Values) 


i) (IR) Cis = 16.5 min 
11) (1S) Cis = 17.4 min 
111) (1R) Trans = 18.5 min 
iv) (1S) Trans = 19.6 min 
B-6 CALCULATION 
(IR)-Isomer ratio of imiprothrin la+ le 100 


technical percent by mass Tak Iba c+ 1d er 


where, 
la = area percentage of (IR)-Cis Isomer; 
Ib = area percentage of (IS)-Cis Isomer; 
Ic = area percentage of (IR)-Trans Isomer; 
Id = area percentage of (IS)-Trans Isomer; and 


mass of the sample taken for the test.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
